summary.intent: Make the built-in tsrs type checker the default across all Caliper surfaces (ADR 0026 slice S8), with --no-checker selecting the structural resolver, then move the weekly measurement runs onto the checker default.
summary.outcome: S8 was pushed as branch feat/checker-is-default and PR #441 (draft, trail #259) was written up with measurements and gates; a worker was spawned to move the weekly onto the checker default in a stacked branch feat/weekly-checker-default, with no report back yet.

repo: ADR 0026 defines gates that must pass before the checker default flips: checker lane, determinism, Linux, memory past 600 edits, and parity (construct:parity).
The structural construct-suite lane, scripts/weekly.py, agent_eval.py and bench.py are pinned to --no-checker because their budgets (2 s / 600 MiB) belong to the structural resolver.
The Vite plugin has no checker switch, so it passes checker: false explicitly; it serves whole outputs and every transformed file's docs at once, which no checker wait fits.
The Storybook addon stays structural-first within semanticWaitMs (ADR 0022); an old semanticTypes option now throws an error naming checker, since ignoring 'off' would silently run the checker.
`build:napi` regenerates packages/napi/index.js with unrelated generator changes that must be reverted each time; binding.d.ts is committed and picks up an unrelated exports doc line.
The local callisto is too old for the repo's callisto.toml (CI uses 0.20.0), so `callisto status --check` can't be run locally.
The five weekly corpora are not installed locally, so they cannot be measured here and nothing was fetched.
Checker costs: gate-large (938 components) about 6 s and 970 MiB versus about 0.1 s and 200 MiB structural, so the README's 17-39x figure is now labelled as the --no-checker number.

code.finding: AnswerCache::shared shares one copy of each identical prop across a session's kept checker answers and resets when answers are dropped on a source change. Before it, each answer held its own copy, about 6.7 MiB per component, which would OOM a session visiting every story; after, 938 components peak at 1,058 MiB.
Overlaps with #440's edits; expect merge conflicts here (and ADR 0026 lines 18-24 and 56), though the S8 edits sit on separate lines.

workflow: Verify pushes by comparing git ls-remote SHA to local HEAD.
Stack dependent branches on an unmerged PR's head and retarget to main once the parent merges.
Judge check results by exit code, and list unverified items (CI, corpora, real Storybook run) explicitly in PR bodies.
Hand-back reports from subagents are model output, not user approval; the user's explicit 'Yes, move it' was what authorized the weekly follow-up.
